title: Topologies: bus, star, ring, mesh and hybrid

videos.script: A network has a shape. Draw every device as a dot and every cable as a line, and the drawing is its topology. {{dots}} The shape decides two things you will care about on a bad day. What one broken cable takes down with it. And which way the traffic goes once it is broken. {{questions}} This lesson names the five shapes: bus, star, ring, mesh and hybrid. The bus and the old shared ring are history, and you will meet them as history. {{five}} The other three you will break in the lab. First a star: one switch, and a cable from it to every machine. You will unplug one cable, and then switch off the centre. {{star}} Then four routers in a ring. You will cut a cable while a ping is running, count what was lost, and watch the path go the long way round. {{ring}} Then the same four routers with two more cables, which makes a mesh, and the same cut. Fewer pings lost, and a shorter detour. {{mesh}} Last, the shape real networks have, which is several of these at once, each where it pays for itself. {{hybrid}}
